Dr. Hongpeng Zhou

Dame Kathleen Ollerenshaw Fellow (Assistant Professor) in the Computer Science Department of the University of Manchester, UK. Dr Zhou leads the HealthAI research group, which focuses on AI for biomedical applications and aims to build interpretable, efficient, effective, and practically useful AI methods that accelerate the translation of AI into biomedical research and uncover the biological mechanisms underlying complex biomedical data. My research interests include machine learning, sparse Bayesian learning, interpretable learning, and bioinformatics.

We are always looking for talented and self-motivated Postdocs, PhDs, and visiting PhDs to join our group (check Here for more details). If you are interested in developing cutting-edge AI methods to tackle fundamental biomedical research challenges, please fill in the PhD application inquiry form. You are also welcome to contact me directly.

More about me:

I was a postdoc research associate at Prof.Magnus Rattray's group - Division of Informatics, Imaging and Data Sciences at the Faculty of Biology, Medicine and Health of the University of Manchester. My research project was to develop machine learning algorithms to reveal biological mechanisms behind single-cell transcriptomics data.

Before the postdoc, I received my PhD degree at the Department of Cognitive Robotics of the Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands, supervised by Prof.Martijn Wisse and Dr.Wei Pan. My PhD work was developing Bayesian deep learning algorithms for neural network compression, neural architecture search, interpretable deep learning and system identification. Please check my PhD thesis "Bayesian deep learning for system identification".

association-and-administration/organizat.text: We are excited to announce a one-day workshop on “Computational & Experimental Spatial Omics”. This event is dedicated to exploring the computational and experimental spatial omics methods as well as establishing an academic community in this space potentially creating new collaborations.
Location: Michael Smith Building, Dover Street, Manchester, M13 9NT
Registration: We aim to host around 80 participants, making it an excellent opportunity for knowledge exchange and networking. Secure your spot by registering on Eventbrite.
